title: Arkansas’ live mascot Tusk VII won’t attend Razorbacks’ season opener due to heat
content:
Arkansas will open its football season Saturday without one notable Razorback on hand: the actual one.

Tusk VII, Arkansas’ live Razorback mascot, will miss what was supposed to be his gameday debut against North Alabama after his veterinarian advised against attending because of heat.

“Looks like Razorback Nation will have to wait a little longer for my game day debut!” the mascot’s official account posted Saturday morning. “At the advice of my veterinarian, I’ll be sitting out today’s game due to the heat.”

The decision comes as temperatures are expected to climb into triple digits in Fayetteville. The National Weather Service issued a heat advisory for the area from noon until 7 p.m. CT Saturday, with a forecast high near 102 degrees and heat-index values potentially reaching 107.

Arkansas and North Alabama are scheduled to kick off at 3:15 p.m. local time at Razorback Stadium, in the middle of the advisory. The game is also the first of head coach Ryan Silverfield’s tenure at Arkansas and the first meeting of the Razorbacks and the Lions, who play in the Football Championship Subdivision.

Tusk VII is the newest member of Arkansas’ longstanding live-mascot lineage. Born Sept. 17, 2025 in Dardanelle, Ark., he weighed 2 pounds, 8 ounces and measured 12 inches long at birth. He is the son of Tusk VI and spent his first year at the Stokes Family Farm in Dardanelle, Ark., before taking over mascot duties in 2026.

The numbered Tusk lineage dates to 1997, when Tusk I was selected as Arkansas’ live mascot. The mascots have since been raised and cared for by the Stokes family, with the current Tusk residing at the family farm near Dardanelle.

Tusk VII’s wait for his first football game will now stretch a little longer.
